name: Galactica 120B
description:
Here is how to read the Galactica 120B config.json. The architecture class is OPTForCausalLM, which is the transformers (or equivalent) module that wires embeddings, attention, the MLP, and the language-modelling head that turns hidden states into next-token logits.

hidden_size is 10,240: that is the width of every residual stream vector. The embedding matrix is therefore 50,000 × 10,240: each token id owns a vector of that width.

num_attention_heads is 80, so each head sees 128 dimensions (10,240 / 80). The ratio test is hidden_size / num_attention_heads = 10240 / 80 = 128. 128 is a multiple of 32 (NVIDIA warp-friendly), and a multiple of 16 (Huawei cube-friendly), and a power of two (Triton / FlashAttention-friendly). From this number alone you cannot name the training chip.

num_hidden_layers is 96: the stack is that many transformer blocks deep.

intermediate_size is 40,960. In a SwiGLU MLP this is the high-dimensional workspace: the 10,240-wide stream is projected up, activated, then projected back. Labs usually round this width to a multiple of 128 or 256 so it tiles on the chip.

max_position_embeddings is 2,048 tokens — the context window in the config. There is no rope_scaling entry, so the rotary positions are used as-is.

vocab_size is 50,000. bos/eos ids, when present, are just two special rows in that table; the padded vocab is often larger than the tokenizer’s real inventory.

torch_dtype is float16.

The copy of config.json is from https://huggingface.co/facebook/Galactica-120B/blob/main/config.json.
